stem: Which choice uses data from the table to show what the final sentence says?
stimulus:
Two middle schools sold the same sugary drinks in their cafeterias. In January, School A installed free water-refill stations in its hallways; School B made no change. The table shows how many sugary drinks each school sold per week. The stations appear to have changed what students bought: ______

Weekly Sugary-Drink Sales
School | Before January | After January
School A (stations added) | 200 | 120
School B (no change) | 200 | 195
choices: Both schools sold 200 sugary drinks per week before January.
School A's sales fell to 120, while School B's sales stayed near 200.
School B's sales fell further after January than School A's sales did.
Sales fell at every school in the district that added refill stations.
explanation: The sentence says the stations changed what students bought, so it needs a difference between the school that got stations and the school that didn't. School A dropped from 200 to 120, and School B barely moved (195). That contrast shows the point. This is the basic move behind SAT questions that give you a table and ask which choice uses the data to complete the passage's sentence.

A.why: This is true, but it shows the two schools were the same before the change. The sentence needs a difference after the change. You picked an accurate reading of the table that doesn't prove the point.

C.why: You reversed the schools. School A fell by 80 drinks and School B fell by only 5.

D.why: The table covers two schools, not every school in the district. You went beyond what the data shows.

stem: Which choice uses data from the table to show what the final sentence says?
stimulus:
After a vaccine dose, the immune system produces antibodies, proteins that help the body recognize an infection. Immunologist Rhea Okafor measured the average antibody level in a group of volunteers once a week for four weeks after vaccination. She concluded that antibody levels peaked in the third week: ______

Average Antibody Level (units per milliliter)
Week | Antibody level
1 | 10
2 | 40
3 | 80
4 | 60
choices: The level rose from 10 in week 1 to 40 in week 2.
The level in week 4 was higher than the level in week 3.
The level peaks in week 3 after every kind of vaccine.
The level was 80 in week 3, higher than in any other week.
explanation: A peak is a maximum, so the sentence needs data showing that week 3 was higher than every other week. At 80, week 3 beats 10, 40 and 60. On the SAT, some of these sentences ask for a highest value, some for a difference and some for a trend. Working out which one before you read the choices is the step this practises.

A.why: This is accurate, but a rise from week 1 to week 2 doesn't show that week 3 was the highest. You matched the topic, not the claim.

B.why: You misread the table. Week 4 (60) is lower than week 3 (80).

C.why: The data comes from one vaccine in one group of volunteers. Nothing in the table covers every kind of vaccine.

stem: Which choice uses data from the table to show what the final sentence says?
stimulus:
Bare steel rusts when exposed to moist air, so engineers often coat it. A team painted steel panels with either Coating X, which is costly, or Coating Y, which costs half as much, and left some panels uncoated. After 30 days outdoors, the team counted rust spots. The cheaper coating protected the steel nearly as well as the costly one: ______

Rust Spots per Panel After 30 Days
Panel | Rust spots
Uncoated | 48
Coating X | 6
Coating Y | 7
choices: Coating X panels had 6 rust spots; Coating Y panels had 7.
Uncoated panels had 48 rust spots; Coating X panels had 6.
Coating Y panels had far fewer rust spots than Coating X panels.
Coating Y panels will stay free of rust spots for many years.
explanation: "Nearly as well" asks for a similarity between the two coatings, with the cheaper one only slightly behind. Six spots versus seven shows exactly that. The words "nearly as well" set how much the data has to show, and reading those limiting words carefully is a habit you need for the real table-completion questions.

B.why: This is true, but it compares Coating X with bare steel. It shows that X works, not that Y is close to X. You picked an accurate comparison of the wrong pair.

C.why: You got the direction wrong. Coating Y had 7 spots, slightly more than Coating X's 6, not far fewer.

D.why: The test ran for 30 days, and Coating Y panels still had 7 spots. The table can't support a claim about many years, or about having no rust at all.

stem: Which choice uses data from the table to show what the final sentence says?
stimulus:
Farms near Mill Creek pump groundwater for irrigation. When pumping removes water faster than rain can refill the underground aquifer, the water table drops. Hydrologists recorded the water level in one Mill Creek well each spring. Their records show that the level declined steadily over the four years: ______

Water Level in Mill Creek Well (meters above sea level)
Year | Water level
2020 | 30
2021 | 28
2022 | 26
2023 | 24
choices: The level in 2022 was 26 meters above sea level.
The level rose by 2 meters every year from 2020 to 2023.
The level fell by 2 meters every year from 2020 to 2023.
The level in every well in the region fell after 2020.
explanation: "Declined steadily" describes a trend, so the sentence needs the change across all the years. It went 30, 28, 26, 24, a drop of 2 meters each year. That shows both the decline and its steadiness. When an SAT completion sentence names a trend, a single number can't finish it. You need the change over time.

A.why: This value is correct, but one year can't show a trend. You need at least two points to show that something declined.

B.why: You read the trend backwards. The numbers go down from 30 to 24, so the level fell.

D.why: The table gives data for one Mill Creek well. It says nothing about the other wells in the region.
